32/G.goal: Explain why interactive XR system development requires a user-centered, structured, iterative lifecycle and how its stages and controlled design-prototype-evaluate loop produce an executable and usable system while managing cost and turnaround time.
32/G.achieves: It provides the foundational development framework used in the course case study, enabling the learner to understand and later implement an XR system with confidence.

32/O1.goal: Explain why usable XR systems require a user-centered, structured software development lifecycle because their interface and interaction design spaces are large.
32/O1.achieves: It gives the learner the rationale and basic vocabulary for treating XR development as a human-centered design problem before studying specific development stages.

32/O2.goal: Explain why interactive XR systems need an iterative lifecycle and how its stages, design-prototype-evaluate loop, and limits on broader iteration establish requirements, implementation, and usability while controlling cost and turnaround time.
32/O2.achieves: It gives the learner a framework for following the case study and for planning the development, evaluation, and controlled iteration of an XR system.
